stem.en: A trial balance is:

options.en: A part of the balance sheet
A statement of ledger balances prepared on a particular date
An account in the ledger
A subsidiary book

explanation.en: A trial balance is a statement (not an account) listing the debit and credit balances of all ledger accounts on a given date.

stem.en: Which of the following accounts normally has a credit balance?

options.en: Drawings
Bills payable
Salaries
Bills receivable

explanation.en: Bills payable is a liability, and liabilities have credit balances. Drawings, salaries and bills receivable have debit balances.

stem.en: The main objective of preparing a trial balance is to:

options.en: Check the arithmetical accuracy of ledger posting
Show the financial position
Record transactions in the journal
Find the net profit

explanation.en: Agreement of the trial balance shows that, arithmetically, every debit has an equal credit in the ledger.

stem.en: Returns inwards (sales returns) is shown in the trial balance on the:

options.en: Debit side
It is not shown
Either side
Credit side

explanation.en: Returns inwards reduce sales, so the sales returns account has a debit balance.

stem.en: Under the balance method, a trial balance is prepared using:

options.en: The net balance of every account
The totals of both sides of every account
Only the personal accounts
Only the cash and bank balances

explanation.en: The balance method lists only the closing (net) balance of each ledger account; it is the most widely used method.

stem.en: Excluding capital, the debit balances of a trial balance total ₹2,40,000 and the credit balances total ₹1,65,000. Capital is:

explanation.en: Capital is a credit balance, so it equals the shortfall on the credit side: 2,40,000 − 1,65,000 = ₹75,000.

stem.en: Which of the following appears on the debit side of a trial balance?

options.en: Outstanding salaries
Sales
Discount received
Discount allowed

explanation.en: Discount allowed is a loss (expense) of the business, so it has a debit balance.

stem.en: In a trial balance, drawings of ₹5,000 were wrongly shown on the credit side and returns outwards of ₹2,000 on the debit side. The wrong totals were: debit ₹97,000, credit ₹1,03,000. The correct agreed total is:
Furniture purchased for office use was debited to the purchases account. This is an error of:

options.en: Compensating nature
Principle
Commission
Omission

explanation.en: A capital item (furniture) was treated as a revenue item (purchases of goods), which violates accounting principles.

stem.en: Which of the following errors does NOT affect the agreement of the trial balance?

options.en: Wrong totalling of the sales book
Posting an amount to the wrong side of an account
Omitting to post one side of an entry
A transaction omitted completely from the journal

explanation.en: If a transaction is not recorded at all, both the debit and the credit are missing, so the trial balance still agrees.

stem.en: Errors that cancel each other's effect on the trial balance are called:

options.en: Errors of omission
Compensating errors
Errors of carrying forward
Errors of principle

explanation.en: A compensating error is offset by another error of the same amount on the opposite side, so the trial balance agrees.

stem.en: Credit sales of ₹5,000 to Mohan were posted to Sohan's account. This is:

options.en: An error of commission that does not affect the trial balance
An error that makes the trial balance disagree
An error of principle
An error of complete omission

explanation.en: The amount was debited correctly, but to a wrong personal account of the same class. Debits still equal credits.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Agreement of the trial balance is not conclusive proof of the accuracy of accounts.
Reason (R): Some errors, such as errors of complete omission and compensating errors, do not affect the agreement of the trial balance.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true, and R explains A: because certain errors leave the totals equal, a balanced trial balance can still hide mistakes.

stem.en: Repairs to building ₹2,000 were debited to the building account. The rectifying entry is:

options.en: Building A/c Dr ₹2,000 To Suspense A/c ₹2,000
Repairs A/c Dr ₹2,000 To Building A/c ₹2,000
Building A/c Dr ₹2,000 To Repairs A/c ₹2,000
Repairs A/c Dr ₹2,000 To Cash A/c ₹2,000

explanation.en: Building was wrongly debited, so credit Building; Repairs should have been debited, so debit Repairs.

stem.en: Salary of ₹5,000 paid to Mr. Arun (an employee) was debited to his personal account. The rectifying entry is:

options.en: Suspense A/c Dr To Arun A/c ₹5,000
Arun A/c Dr To Salary A/c ₹5,000
Salary A/c Dr To Arun A/c ₹5,000
Salary A/c Dr To Cash A/c ₹5,000

explanation.en: Cancel the wrong debit by crediting Arun's account and debit the correct account, Salary.

stem.en: A purchase of ₹7,000 from Ravi was recorded in the purchases book as ₹700. The rectifying entry is:

options.en: Purchases A/c Dr To Ravi A/c ₹6,300
Ravi A/c Dr To Purchases A/c ₹6,300
Purchases A/c Dr To Suspense A/c ₹6,300
Purchases A/c Dr To Ravi A/c ₹7,700

explanation.en: The wrong amount went to both accounts, so the difference 7,000 − 700 = ₹6,300 is debited to Purchases and credited to Ravi.

stem.en: Goods of ₹1,500 returned by Anil (a customer) were entered in the purchases returns book. The rectifying entry is:

options.en: Anil A/c Dr ₹3,000 To Sales Returns A/c ₹1,500 and Purchases Returns A/c ₹1,500
Sales Returns A/c Dr ₹1,500 and Purchases Returns A/c Dr ₹1,500 To Anil A/c ₹3,000
Purchases Returns A/c Dr ₹1,500 To Sales Returns A/c ₹1,500
Sales Returns A/c Dr ₹1,500 To Anil A/c ₹1,500

explanation.en: Wrong entry: Anil Dr, Purchases Returns Cr ₹1,500. Correct: Sales Returns Dr, Anil Cr ₹1,500. To correct, reverse the wrong entry and pass the right one: Sales Returns Dr 1,500, Purchases Returns Dr 1,500, To Anil 3,000.

stem.en: The rectifying entry for error (iii) is:

options.en: Machinery A/c Dr To Suspense A/c ₹2,000
Wages A/c Dr To Machinery A/c ₹2,000
Machinery A/c Dr To Wages A/c ₹2,000
Suspense A/c Dr To Wages A/c ₹2,000

explanation.en: Installation wages are part of the cost of the machine (capital expenditure). This two-sided error of principle does not touch the suspense account.

passage.en: Meena, the accountant of Sharada Traders, found that the trial balance on 31 March 2025 did not agree: the debit side was short by ₹1,800. She placed the difference in a suspense account and prepared the final accounts. Later she found three errors: (i) the purchases book was undercast by ₹1,000; (ii) a credit sale of ₹800 to Ravi was not posted to Ravi's account; (iii) wages of ₹2,000 paid for installing a new machine were debited to the wages account.

stem.en: If the debit total of a trial balance exceeds the credit total by ₹2,000, the suspense account will be:

options.en: Shown on the credit side with ₹2,000
Not opened
Shown on the debit side with ₹2,000
Shown on both sides with ₹1,000

explanation.en: The suspense account is placed on the shorter side, here the credit side, to make the totals agree.

stem.en: After the trial balance was prepared, it was found that the sales book was undercast by ₹1,000. The rectifying entry is:

options.en: Suspense A/c Dr To Sales A/c ₹1,000
Sales A/c Dr To Suspense A/c ₹1,000
Suspense A/c Dr To Debtors A/c ₹1,000
Debtors A/c Dr To Sales A/c ₹1,000

explanation.en: Sales was credited ₹1,000 short (a one-sided error), so credit Sales and debit Suspense.

stem.en: A trial balance whose credit side was short by ₹1,200 was balanced with a suspense account. Later it was found that the purchases book was overcast by ₹700 and rent of ₹500 paid was not posted to the rent account. After rectifying these two errors, the suspense account shows:

options.en: No balance
A credit balance of ₹2,400
A debit balance of ₹1,000
A credit balance of ₹1,000

explanation.en: Suspense opens with Cr ₹1,200. Purchases overcast: Suspense Dr 700 To Purchases. Rent omitted: Rent Dr 500 To Suspense. Balance = 1,200 + 500 − 700 = ₹1,000 credit; more errors remain to be found.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): A suspense account is closed once all the errors that caused the difference in the trial balance are located and rectified.
Reason (R): A suspense account is a permanent account that appears in the balance sheet every year.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true. R is false: the suspense account is a temporary account; it appears in the balance sheet only while some errors remain undetected.

stem.en: In the trial balance, the suspense account will appear on the:

options.en: Debit side with ₹1,800
Credit side with ₹1,800
Debit side with ₹1,000
Credit side with ₹800

explanation.en: The debit side was short by ₹1,800, so suspense is put on the debit side. Errors (i) and (ii) are each debit-side shortages: 1,000 + 800 = ₹1,800.

passage.en: Meena, the accountant of Sharada Traders, found that the trial balance on 31 March 2025 did not agree: the debit side was short by ₹1,800. She placed the difference in a suspense account and prepared the final accounts. Later she found three errors: (i) the purchases book was undercast by ₹1,000; (ii) a credit sale of ₹800 to Ravi was not posted to Ravi's account; (iii) wages of ₹2,000 paid for installing a new machine were debited to the wages account.
